why: The winds aloft a leg flies in, read from the winds-aloft grid by level and by hour (engine/crates/weather/src/aloft_grid.rs, wind_aloft_at), held by the engine (engine/facade/tests/aloft_grid.rs) and the planner (services/planner/tests_wingtip/test_winds_aloft.py). Each level's wind is its east and north parts, kt, toward where it blows: u 20, v 0 is a wind from 270 at 20 kt. The expected answers are worked by hand: linear between levels and between hours (as a pilot reads between the FB's levels, FAA-H-8083-28B 27.2.1.1.1), past the lowest level the temperature keeping its difference from a standard day (ICAO Doc 7488's 1.9812 C a thousand feet).

cases.why: halfway between 3,000 and 6,000 ft: the speed and the temperature halfway
halfway between two hours two hours apart: the speed and the temperature halfway
a level under the ground (no wind) is left out: under the lowest level left, its wind, and its temperature carried down at the standard lapse rate (5 + 2 x 1.9812)
after the last hour, the last hour's
no hours: no wind and no temperature known, never calm
